1 tsp. Dijon mustard
SALAD:
1 lg. head romaine lettuce, torn into bite-sized pieces (about 10 c.)
1/4 c. sweetened dried cranberries
1 apple, cubed
4 oz. (1 c.) shredded Swiss cheese
1 pear, cubed (Anjou or Bose)
1 c. cashews
In blender container or food processor bowl with metal blade, combine sugar, lemon juice, onion, mustard and salt. Cover. Process until blended. With machine running, add oil in slow steady stream, processing until thick and smooth. (If you don't have a blender or food processor, may use bowl and wire whisk.) Add poppy seeds last and process a few seconds to mix.
In large serving bowl, combine all salad ingredients, toss to mix. Pour dressing over salad just before serving, as will wilt lettuce. Toss to coat.
Yield: 12 (1-cup) servings.
Nutritional Information Per Serving: 280 calories. Dietary Exchange: 1 starch, 1 vegetable, 4 fats.
Dawn Mayer
organization: Alpha Zeta. Wilson   Chapter (Iowa State University)

title: Salami and Shells Salad
full_text:
7 oz. sm. pasta shells
1 (6 oz.) block Mozzarella cheese, cut in thin strips (or 1 c. shredded)
1 c. halved cherry tomatoes
1 c. halved ripe olives
1/2 c. chopped green pepper
4 oz. salami, cut in thin strips
DRESSING:
1/3 c. oil
1 tsp. dried basil
3 T. red wine vinegar
1 tsp. oregano leaves
1 tsp. salt
1/4 tsp. garlic powder
Cook pasta according to directions; drain and rinse in cold water. Place in large bowl, add remaining salad ingredients. Combine dressing ingredients in a jar with a tight-fitting lid. Shake well. Pour over salad and toss to coat.
Note: Best if made ahead of serving time so dressing can combine with salad.
Dawn Mayer
organization: Alpha Zeta. Wilson   Chapter (Iowa State University)

title: Crunchy Tuna or Chicken Salad
full_text:
2 (6 oz.) cans water-packed tuna or chicken
1 (8 oz.) can bamboo shoots, drained & cut
1/4 c. chopped onion
1 c. Miracle Whip
1/2 c. chopped celery
1 T. lemon juice
1 (8 oz.) can water chestnuts, drained & sliced
1 tsp. dill weed
1/8 tsp. pepper
Combine and chill.
Jennie Hansen
organization: Alpha Zeta. Wilson   Chapter (Iowa State University)

title: Pink Salad
full_text:
1 pkg. cherry Jello
1 c. crushed pineapple
1 c. boiling water
Nutmeats
1/4 c. sugar
1 c. cream or condensed milk
1 (3 oz.) pkg. cream cheese
Dissolve Jello, sugar and boiling water. Add and beat with mixer the cream cheese, cream and nutmeats. Chill in refrigerator.
Jennie Hansen
organization: Alpha Zeta. Wilson   Chapter (Iowa State University)

title: Seven-Layer Salad
full_text:
Shredded lettuce
1 (10 oz.) box frozen peas, cooked
1/2 lb. bacon, crumbled
3/4 c. sour cream
6 hard-boiled eggs, sliced
3/4 c. Miracle Whip
1/2 c. onion, chopped
1 c. grated cheese
Place first 5 ingredients as listed in a 9x13-inch pan. Mix sour cream and Miracle Whip, and spread over salad. Top with cheese.
Andy Jennett
organization: Alpha Zeta. Wilson   Chapter (Iowa State University)

title: Nutty Broccoli Salad
full_text:
1 (3 oz.) pkg. chicken Ramen noodles
1 (16 oz.) pkg. broccoli slaw mix
2 c. sliced green onions (2 bunches)
1 1/2 c. broccoli florets
1 (6 oz.) can ripe olives, drained & halved
1 c. sunflower kernels, toasted
1/2 c. slivered almonds, toasted
1/2 c. vinegar
1/2 c. sugar
1/2 c. olive oil
Set aside the noodle seasoning packet. Crush the noodles and place in a large bowl. Add the slaw mix, onion, broccoli, olives, sunflower kernels and almonds.
In a jar with a tight-fitting lid, combine sugar, vinegar, oil and contents of seasoning packet; shake well. Drizzle over salad and toss to coat. Serve immediately. Yield: 16 servings.
Holly Lenz
organization: Alpha Zeta. Wilson   Chapter (Iowa State University)

title: Cabbage Slaw
full_text:
2 heads cabbage
2 to 3 onions
1 c. vinegar
1 c. sugar
3/4 c. oil
2 T. salt
2 T. celery seed
1 T. dry mustard
Chop cabbage into slivers. Chop onions. Bring vinegar, sugar, oil, salt, celery seed and dry mustard to a boil. Pour liquid over cabbage and onion. Place salad into sealed container and keep in refrigerator overnight.
Holly Lenz
organization: Alpha Zeta. Wilson   Chapter (Iowa State University)

title: Fruit Salad for 20
full_text:
2 lg. cans pineapple
3 cans mandarin oranges
1 lg. can peaches
4 bananas
1 (6 oz.) pkg. strawberry Jello
Strawberries
2 regular pkg. vanilla pudding
2 T. tapioca
Drain fruit. Measure 4 cups juice. Mix Jello, pudding, juices and tapioca. Cook until thick. Let cool completely. Mix over fruit.
Alyce Gehling
organization: Alpha Zeta. Wilson   Chapter (Iowa State University)

title: Winter Fruit Salad
full_text:
DRESSING:
1/2 c. sugar
2 tsp. finely-chopped onion
1/3 c. lemon juice
1 tsp. dry mustard
1/2 tsp. salt
2/3 c. oil
1 T. poppy seeds
SALAD:
About 10 c. romaine lettuce
1 c. grated Parmesan cheese
1 c. cashews
1/4 c. sweetened dried cranberries
1 apple, diced
1 pear, cubed
Whisk dressing ingredients together in small bowl and set aside. Combine all salad ingredients; toss to mix. Pour dressing over salad.
Molly Mayer
organization: Alpha Zeta. Wilson   Chapter (Iowa State University)

title: Seven-Layer Salad
full_text:
1 head lettuce
1 can peas, drained
1 c. shredded cheese
1 c. diced celery
2 c. mayonnaise
1 lb. bacon, cooked & crumbled
1/2 c. diced onions
Wash and shred lettuce (or use bagged lettuce). Place in a 9x13-inch pan. Layer peas over the top. Layer celery, then onions. Spread mayonnaise for the next layer. Sprinkle cheese over top for the next layer and lastly, crumble bacon over the top. Yield: 12 servings.
This makes 12 servings unless your family is like mine and loves salad, then it feeds six.
Drew Simonsen
organization: Alpha Zeta. Wilson   Chapter (Iowa State University)

title: Good and Tasty Pasta Salad
full_text:
1 (1 lb.) box penne pasta, cooked according to pkg. directions
2 c. cherry tomatoes, halved
2 sm. cucumbers, sliced & quartered
2 T. oil
1 1/2 c. white balsamic vinegar
1 tsp. salt
1/2 tsp. pepper
1 tsp. garlic powder
1 tsp. mustard (dried, ground)
Cook pasta according to box directions. Drain. Drizzle with oil; toss to coat and let cool slightly. Mix all other ingredients well. Put pasta in large bowl; pour dressing over pasta, tomatoes and cucumbers. Refrigerate for at least 4 hours before serving. (Mix well several times while refrigerating.)
Note: Stores well for 2 to 3 days.
Michelle Euken
organization: Alpha Zeta. Wilson   Chapter (Iowa State University)

title: Southwest Cornbread Salad
full_text:
3/4 c. ranch salad dressing
1/4 c. chopped red onion
3/4 tsp. curry powder
1/4 c. chopped fresh cilantro
15 slices bacon, cooked
1 (11 oz.) can Green Giant mexicorn (whole kernel corn with red & green peppers), drained
8 c. cubed cornbread
1 med. tomato, diced
In 1-cup glass measuring cup, combine salad dressing and curry powder; mix well. Let stand 5 to 10 minutes to blend flavors.
Meanwhile, cook bacon as directed on package until crisp. Drain on paper towel; crumble.
In large bowl, combine cornbread, tomato, onion, cilantro and corn. Add bacon and dressing mixture. Toss gently to coat. Yield: 15 servings.
Michelle Euken
organization: Alpha Zeta. Wilson   Chapter (Iowa State University)

title: Pesto Chicken-Potato Salad
full_text:
2 lb. Yukon Gold potatoes, cut into 3/4-inch cubes (about 6 potatoes)
2 c. chopped deli rotisserie-cooked chicken
1 ctn. refrigerated pesto
1 c. sliced celery
1/2 c. mayonnaise
1/2 c. sliced green onions
2 T. cider vinegar
2 med. tomatoes, chopped
2 tsp. Dijon mustard
Boston leaf lettuce (opt.)
3/4 tsp. salt
In 3 1/2-quart saucepan, combine potatoes and enough water to cover potatoes by 1 inch. Bring to a boil over medium-high heat. Reduce heat to medium; cover and cook 12 to 15 minutes, or until tender. Drain. Cool 15 minutes, or until slightly cooled.
Meanwhile, in large serving bowl, combine pesto, mayonnaise, vinegar, mustard and salt. Mix well. Add cooked potatoes and all remaining ingredients, except lettuce, to pesto mixture; toss gently until evenly coated. Cover and refrigerate for at least 2 hours, or overnight to blend flavors. If desired, serve on lettuce-lined plates. Yield: 6 servings.
Michelle Euken
organization: Alpha Zeta. Wilson   Chapter (Iowa State University)

title: Fruit Salad with Orange Poppy Seed Dressing
full_text:
1/4 c. orange juice
1/2 c. canola or corn oil
3 T. cider vinegar
1 T. poppy seeds
3 T. Dijon mustard
6 c. fruit (orange segments, cantaloupe, watermelon, honeydew, blueberries, blackberries, grapes, strawberry slices, pomegranate, etc.)
2 T. honey
1 T. Worcestershire sauce
1 tsp. grated orange peel
1/2 tsp. salt
To prepare dressing, place juice, vinegar, mustard, honey, Worcestershire sauce, orange peel and salt in blender or food processor. Cover and process until well blended. Gradually add oil in a steady stream, processing until very smooth. Stir in poppy seeds. Spoon dressing over fruit just before serving. Yield: about 6 servings.
Michelle Euken
organization: Alpha Zeta. Wilson   Chapter (Iowa State University)

title: Chicken Mousse
full_text:
Scald 1 cup milk, cream or chicken broth. Beat yolks of 3 eggs slightly. Add 1/4 teaspoon salt and dash of paprika. Cook until it coats a spoon. Remove from fire and add 1/4 package gelatin softened in 1/4 cup cold water. Stir in 1 1/2 cups cooked chicken breasts chopped as fine as possible. Stir over ice water until it begins to set, then fold in 1 cup whipped cream. Set in molds and serve with mayonnaise dressing.
MRS. J. REED LANE.
organization: Trinity Cathedral (Davenport, Iowa). Trinity Guild; Trinity Cathedral (Davenport, Iowa). St. Margaret's Guild

title: Cheese Salad
full_text:
Ten (10) cakes Blue Ribbon cheese, 1/2 pint coffee cream, 1/2 pint whipped cream, 1 package candied cherries, 1/2 green pepper chopped, 1/2 cup English walnuts chopped, 1 glass preserved fruit. Mash cheese with silver fork till crumbed. Whip coffee cream and skim off froth and add to cheese to thin it. Then chopped cherries, nuts, green pepper. Add mustard, salt, paprika, sugar and red pepper to taste. Add 1/2 envelope gelatin which has been dissolved in a little hot milk and cooled. Add whipped cream and mold. Serve from a ring mold with preserved fruit bar-le-duc or brandied jam in center.
MRS. D. J. McCARTHY.
organization: Trinity Cathedral (Davenport, Iowa). Trinity Guild; Trinity Cathedral (Davenport, Iowa). St. Margaret's Guild

title: Cucumber, Pineapple Salad
full_text:
One-half (1/2) box gelatin, 1/2 cup cold water, pinch of salt, juice of 1 lemon and 1/3 cup vinegar, 2 cups hot water and 1/2 cup sugar. Soak gelatin in cold water until soft, then add hot water and other ingredients, also a little vegetable green coloring matter. Set away and when it commences to congeal add 1 cup shredded pineapple from which juice has been drained and 1 cup chopped cucumber. Mold and serve with a sweet and cooked salad dressing.
MRS. HARRY SPENCER.
organization: Trinity Cathedral (Davenport, Iowa). Trinity Guild; Trinity Cathedral (Davenport, Iowa). St. Margaret's Guild

title: Fruit Salad
full_text:
Grape fruit, oranges and pineapple in mold and sprinkle with pearl onion (can be omitted). Dissolve 1 1/4 package of gelatin in 1/2 cup cold water and add 1 1/2 cups cold water or 2 cups fruit juice. When hard put on lettuce and pour dressing over it.
MRS. E. P. ADLER.
organization: Trinity Cathedral (Davenport, Iowa). Trinity Guild; Trinity Cathedral (Davenport, Iowa). St. Margaret's Guild

title: Fruit Salad Dressing
full_text:
One (1) can of pineapple, 3/4, cup sugar, 2 tablespoons butter, 2 eggs, 1 tablespoon flour, and 1 cup whipped cream. Heat the pineapple juice, cream, butter and flour together, yolks of 2 eggs beaten, then the whites beaten very stiff. Pour the warm pineapple juice in this and heat until thick, stirring constantly. When cold add whipped cream and a cup of marshmallows cut up, some pecans, and lemon or orange juice or a little gingerale.
MRS. E. P. ADLER.
organization: Trinity Cathedral (Davenport, Iowa). Trinity Guild; Trinity Cathedral (Davenport, Iowa). St. Margaret's Guild

title: Gelatin Salad
full_text:
One (1) tablespoon gelatin dissolved in 1/4 cup cold water. Pour over this 1 1/2 cups boiling water. Add 1/4 cup sugar, 1/4 cup vinegar, 2 tablespoons lemon juice and 1 teaspoon salt. Strain and cool. Add 1 cup diced celery, 2 chopped pimentoes, a small bottle stuffed olives, celery cabbage may be chopped and added. Pour into molds and chill and serve with mayonnaise dressing.
MRS. MARTIN SMITH.
organization: Trinity Cathedral (Davenport, Iowa). Trinity Guild; Trinity Cathedral (Davenport, Iowa). St. Margaret's Guild

title: Grapefruit Jelly Salad
full_text:
One-half (1/2) box Knox's sparkling gelatin, 1 cup cold water, 1 cup sugar, 1 cup boiling water, juice of 1 lemon and 2 cups grapefruit juice and pulp. Soak gelatin in cold water 5 minutes. Dissolve with the boiling water and add sugar. Stir until all is dissolved and add lemon juice. Strain liquid and cool. Then add grapefruit juice and pulp and when gelatin is ready to set mold. Turn out of molds and serve on lettuce.
MRS. ISAAC DEUTSCH.
organization: Trinity Cathedral (Davenport, Iowa). Trinity Guild; Trinity Cathedral (Davenport, Iowa). St. Margaret's Guild

title: Nut and Pickle Salad
full_text:
Two and one-half (2 1/2) tablespoons granulated gelatin, 1 cup English walnut meats, 2 cups sweet pickles, 2 cups cold water, 12 cloves, 2 cups sugar, 1 cup cider vinegar (medium strength) mayonnaise, lettuce. Boil together vinegar, sugar and cloves till the mixture threads, remove from the heat and add the gelatin which should have been soaked in cold water. Cool and when beginning to set, stir in the nut meats broken and the pickles sliced thin. Pour into individual molds and set aside for a few hours to stiffen. Serve on lettuce with a garnish of mayonnaise. Will serve 15.
MRS. GORDON F. HARKNESS.
organization: Trinity Cathedral (Davenport, Iowa). Trinity Guild; Trinity Cathedral (Davenport, Iowa). St. Margaret's Guild

title: Pineapple-Cheese Salad
full_text:
One (1) package Knox's gelatin dissolved in 1 cup cold water, 1 pint boiling water, scant cup sugar, 1 small can grated pineapple, juice 1/2 lemon, 1 1/4 cup yellow cream cheese cut in cubes, 1/2 pint whipping cream. Cook pineapple, sugar and lemon juice 5 minutes. Add boiling water and gelatin. Let stand until thick. Add cheese and whipped cream (beaten). Put on ice. Can be made the day before.
MRS. CHRIS HEUCK.
organization: Trinity Cathedral (Davenport, Iowa). Trinity Guild; Trinity Cathedral (Davenport, Iowa). St. Margaret's Guild

title: Stuffed Green Pepper Salad
full_text:
Remove all seeds from the green peppers and stuff tightly with Blue Ribbon cream cheese which has been mixed thoroughly with cream and chopped pimentoes. Do not make too thin. Let stand in ice-box for several hours or over night. Then slice these stuffed peppers. Put on crisp lettuce leaves and pour over them French dressing.
MRS. C. D. WATERMAN.
organization: Trinity Cathedral (Davenport, Iowa). Trinity Guild; Trinity Cathedral (Davenport, Iowa). St. Margaret's Guild

title: Sweetbread Salad
full_text:
Wash sweetbreads in warm water and put in a stew pan with a little salt and pepper. Pour boiling water over to cover and cook until tender. Drop in ice water to bleach. When cold trim, wipe dry and dice. Mix with equal quantities of celery and boiled French peas. Moisten with French dressing. Serve with mayonnaise.
MRS. J. H. WHITAKER.
organization: Trinity Cathedral (Davenport, Iowa). Trinity Guild; Trinity Cathedral (Davenport, Iowa). St. Margaret's Guild

title: Fruit Salad
full_text:
Two (2) cups white cherries, halved, 2 cups pineapple, cut in pieces, 2 oranges cut in pieces, 2 cups marshmallows quartered. Combine with salad dressing made as follows: 2 eggs beaten, 4 tablespoons vinegar, 4 tablespoons sugar, 2 tablespoons butter, 1 cup whipping cream. Mix sugar with well beaten eggs and add vinegar and cook until it thickens, stirring constantly. Add butter, cool and add whipped cream. Serves 12 to 14.
MRS. W. F. KREBILL.
organization: Trinity Cathedral (Davenport, Iowa). Trinity Guild; Trinity Cathedral (Davenport, Iowa). St. Margaret's Guild

title: Cranberry-Orange Salad
full_text:
One (1) package lemon jello dissolved in 1 cup boiling water. Let thicken slightly and then add 1 1/2 cups raw cranberries and 1 orange which have been ground together.
MRS. ALBERT BEHNKE.
organization: Trinity Cathedral (Davenport, Iowa). Trinity Guild; Trinity Cathedral (Davenport, Iowa). St. Margaret's Guild

title: Cabbage and Apple Salad
full_text:
Finely shredded cabbage, chopped apples, nut meats, mayonnaise. Mix well toegther.
MRS. WM. POHLMANN.
organization: Trinity Cathedral (Davenport, Iowa). Trinity Guild; Trinity Cathedral (Davenport, Iowa). St. Margaret's Guild

title: Snow Mound Salad
full_text:
One-half (1/2) pint whipped cream, 1 pint shredded cabbage, 1 can pineapple, 1 small box marshmallows, 3 tablespoons mayonnaise. Mix all ingredients together and let stand a few hours.
MRS. W. G. HENLE.
organization: Trinity Cathedral (Davenport, Iowa). Trinity Guild; Trinity Cathedral (Davenport, Iowa). St. Margaret's Guild

title: Lime Jelly Ring. Individual Service
full_text:
Two (2) tablespoons crushed orange or pineapple, 1 individual lime jelly ring, 1/2 cup cottage cheese, 2 tablespoons chopped walnuts, 3 sections orange, 1 strawberry, 6 tablespoons shredded lettuce, 1 tablespoon French dressing. Make cottage cheese into 3 balls, roll in chopped nuts. Peel orange and cut into sections. Cover plate with lettuce. Place lime jelly ring in center and fill with fruit and strawberry on top. Arrange sections of orange and cheese balls alternately. Put French dressing over fruit.
MRS. W. G. HENLE.
organization: Trinity Cathedral (Davenport, Iowa). Trinity Guild; Trinity Cathedral (Davenport, Iowa). St. Margaret's Guild

title: Beet-Celery Salad
full_text:
One (1) package lemon jello, 3/4 cup beet juice, 1/2 cup boiling water, 3 tablespoons vinegar, 1/2 cup sugar, 3/4 cup diced celery, 1 cup diced beets. Pour boiling water over lemon jello and stir until thoroughly dissolved. Add beet juice, vinegar and sugar and let this mixture stand until it starts to jell, then add diced celery and diced beets. Serves 6.
MRS. ALBERT BEHNKE.
organization: Trinity Cathedral (Davenport, Iowa). Trinity Guild; Trinity Cathedral (Davenport, Iowa). St. Margaret's Guild

title: Apple Salad
full_text:
One (1) package lemon jello, 1 small jar stuffed olives, 1 small can pineapple tid-bits, 1/2 cup diced celery, 4 or 5 solid eating apples, red cinnamon candy. Scoop out about 36 balls from the apples and place in boiling water into which red cinnamon candy has been placed. Let boil until the apple balls have a nice tinge of red. Add the apples, celery, pineapple and olives, which have been sliced, to the jello, and pour into individual molds.
MRS. WM. POHLMANN, Jr.
organization: Trinity Cathedral (Davenport, Iowa). Trinity Guild; Trinity Cathedral (Davenport, Iowa). St. Margaret's Guild

title: Cottage Cheese-Pineapple Salad
full_text:
One (1) package lemon jello, 1 1/2 cups water or pineapple juice, 1 cup crushed pineapple, well drained, 2 cups cottage cheese also well drained, 1/4 pound ground almonds. Chopped chives and green peppers may be added. Fills large mold.
MRS. H. R. LAFFERTY.
organization: Trinity Cathedral (Davenport, Iowa). Trinity Guild; Trinity Cathedral (Davenport, Iowa). St. Margaret's Guild

title: Prune and Pineapple Salad
full_text:
Twelve (12) Italian prunes (large can), 3/4 cup diced pineapple, 1 tablespoon gelatin, 1/2 cup cold water, 3 tablespoons lemon juice. Drain the fruit well. Measure the pineapple juice, add enough prune juice to make 1 1/2 cups liquid. Heat the juice, add the gelatin, which has been soaked in cold water, stir until dissolved, add lemon juice. Pour one-half liquid into mold. When it congeals add prunes and pineapple and remainder of liquid. When hardened, unmold and serve on crisp lettuce leaves.
MRS. LEE WHITE.
organization: Trinity Cathedral (Davenport, Iowa). Trinity Guild; Trinity Cathedral (Davenport, Iowa). St. Margaret's Guild

title: Cherry Salad
full_text:
One (1) can black cherries, pitted and stuffed with nuts. Add to 1 package orange jello which has been made with cherry juice. Serve with whipped cream and mayonnaise dressing.
MRS. W. G. HENLE.
organization: Trinity Cathedral (Davenport, Iowa). Trinity Guild; Trinity Cathedral (Davenport, Iowa). St. Margaret's Guild

title: Cheese Salad
full_text:
Two (2) packages lemon jello, 1 package Philadelphia cream cheese, thinned to consistency of cream, with pineapple juice, 1/2 pint whipped cream, diced pineapple, sliced stuffed olives. Prepare jello and let thicken slightly. Add other ingredients and allow to chill and set thoroughly.
MRS. PHILLIP T. STEFFEN.
organization: Trinity Cathedral (Davenport, Iowa). Trinity Guild; Trinity Cathedral (Davenport, Iowa). St. Margaret's Guild

title: Tomato Surprise
full_text:
Six (6) medium sized firm tomatoes (cut 6 wedges almost through so they open into the form of a flower). Fill with the following: 1 pint cottage cheese, 1 or 2 pieces chopped celery, 1/4 cup finely chopped parsley, a little chopped onion may be added if desired. Mix with mayonnaise.
MRS. W. G. HENLE.
organization: Trinity Cathedral (Davenport, Iowa). Trinity Guild; Trinity Cathedral (Davenport, Iowa). St. Margaret's Guild

title: Tomato Shrimp Salad
full_text:
One (1) quart canned tomatoes, 1 1/4 cups water, 1 1/2 teaspoons salt, 1/4 teaspoon pepper, 4 cloves, 1 bayleaf, 1 tablespoon sugar, 1/2 teaspoon mustard, 2 tablespoons gelatin, 1 1/2 cups shrimp, 1/2 cup finely diced celery, 1/4 cup diced green pepper, 1 small onion minced. Cook tomatoes, water, salt, pepper, cloves, bayleaf, sugar, mustard and onion for 15 minutes. Strain and pour over the gelatin which has been softened in 1/4 cup cold water. Cool, add shrimp, celery and green pepper. Pour into a ring mold and chill. Serve with lettuce and mayonnaise.
MRS. WALTER A. PRIESTER.
organization: Trinity Cathedral (Davenport, Iowa). Trinity Guild; Trinity Cathedral (Davenport, Iowa). St. Margaret's Guild

title: Tomato Aspic
full_text:
Two and one-quarter (2 1/4) cups canned tomatoes, 1 package strawberry jello, 1 3/4 teaspoons onion pulp, 2 1/4 teaspoons horseradish, 1 3/4 teaspoons salt, dash of cayenne. Bring tomatoes to a boil. Add jello. Dissolve and add horseradish, onion, salt and pepper. Strain and mold.
MRS. CLARENCE VERNON.
organization: Trinity Cathedral (Davenport, Iowa). Trinity Guild; Trinity Cathedral (Davenport, Iowa). St. Margaret's Guild

title: Simple Tomato Aspic
full_text:
Two (2) packages lemon jello, 2 14 ounce cans tomato juice cocktail, 4 ounces hot water. Add to jello when boiling. Season and pour in ring mold. Add asparagus tips and chopped olives or shrimps and diced celery. Carrots, celery, and cucumbers may also be used.
MRS. JAMES CRATON.
organization: Trinity Cathedral (Davenport, Iowa). Trinity Guild; Trinity Cathedral (Davenport, Iowa). St. Margaret's Guild

title: Celery and Prune Salad
full_text:
One (1) cup chopped prunes, cooked, 1 cup chopped celery, 1 cup nuts, 6 pieces lettuce, 1 cup salad dressing. Mix the prunes, celery, and nuts. Arrange on lettuce leaves, add dressing and serve.
MRS. WALTER JONES.
organization: Trinity Cathedral (Davenport, Iowa). Trinity Guild; Trinity Cathedral (Davenport, Iowa). St. Margaret's Guild

title: Grapefruit Salad
full_text:
Halve and remove inside of fruit, strain the juice and cover with: 2 tablespoons sugar, 2 tablespoons chopped mint cherries, 2 tablespoons chopped almonds, 1 tablespoon grape juice. Chill thoroughly. Serve in grapefruit shells with sprig of mint.
MRS. LEE WHITE.
organization: Trinity Cathedral (Davenport, Iowa). Trinity Guild; Trinity Cathedral (Davenport, Iowa). St. Margaret's Guild

title: Grape and Pear Salad
full_text:
Use halves of canned pears. Wipe pears dry, coat pears with Philadelphia cream cheese, place halves of white grapes on pears. Serve on grape leaves. Serve mayonnaise separately.
MRS. LEE WHITE.
organization: Trinity Cathedral (Davenport, Iowa). Trinity Guild; Trinity Cathedral (Davenport, Iowa). St. Margaret's Guild

title: Twenty-four Hour Salad
full_text:
Four (4) yolks of egg, 1/4 cup of cream, 1 teaspoon sugar, pinch salt, juice of 1 lemon. Put above in pan and let come to boil. One can sliced pineapple cut in small pieces, 1/2 pound marshmallows cut in pieces, 1 pound red grapes, seeded and cut in pieces, 1 cup of whipping cream. Add these to dressing and let stand 24 hours.
MRS. W. E. BETTENDORF.
organization: Trinity Cathedral (Davenport, Iowa). Trinity Guild; Trinity Cathedral (Davenport, Iowa). St. Margaret's Guild

title: Cream Cheese-Tomato Salad
full_text:
One (1) can Campbell's tomato soup, 3 packages Philadelphia cream cheese. Melt these together. 1 envelope Knox's plain gelatin dissolved in 1 cup cold water. Add to first mixture and cool. Add 1/2 cup chopped celery, 1/2 onion grated, 1/4 pound almonds ground, 1/2 cucumber ground, 1 cup mayonnaise. Stir entire mixture together and put into individual or 1 large mold to harden. Splendid accompaniment to fish.
MRS. H. R. LAFFERTY.
organization: Trinity Cathedral (Davenport, Iowa). Trinity Guild; Trinity Cathedral (Davenport, Iowa). St. Margaret's Guild

title: Stuffed Tomato and Cheese Salad
full_text:
Peel and remove seeds from desired number of nice firm tomatoes. Beat creamed cottage cheese until light and season with salt, whole ground black pepper and a dash of paprika. Sprinkle a few small pearl onions over the top and serve on shredded lettuce and watercress. Cover with French dressing.
MRS. F. H. FRENCH.
organization: Trinity Cathedral (Davenport, Iowa). Trinity Guild; Trinity Cathedral (Davenport, Iowa). St. Margaret's Guild

title: Shrimp and Pineapple Salad
full_text:
One and one-half (1 1/2) cups fresh cooked or canned shrimp, 1 cup canned or fresh pineapple, diced, 1/8 teaspoon paprika, 2 sprigs chives, chopped, 6 tablespoons French dressing, 1/2 teaspoon salt. Combine shrimp, pineapple, salt, paprika and chives. Chill thoroughly and just before serving pour over the dressing. Toss until well mixed and serve on endive.
MRS. CLARENCE VERNON.
organization: Trinity Cathedral (Davenport, Iowa). Trinity Guild; Trinity Cathedral (Davenport, Iowa). St. Margaret's Guild

title: Crab Salad
full_text:
One (1) pint crab meat, 2 stalks celery, cut fine, 1 hardboiled egg chopped fine, 1 tomato cut in small pieces. Season with salt, pepper and vinegar (diluted with water), 1 tablespoon of mayonnaise dressing. Mix and place in bowl, garnish it with the crisp white leaves of head lettuce. A few capers add to the flavor.
MRS. LEE WHITE.
organization: Trinity Cathedral (Davenport, Iowa). Trinity Guild; Trinity Cathedral (Davenport, Iowa). St. Margaret's Guild

title: German Potato Salad
full_text:
Boil 6 medium sized new potatoes, cool, peel and slice. Cut 5 strips of bacon into small pieces and fry. Mix four tablespoons vinegar with 4 tablespoons water and bring to a boil. Beat a whole egg and slowly stir the vinegar and water into this. Cut up green onions and a little celery and add to the potatoes. Pour egg and vinegar mixture over the potatoes. Add bacon and fat, salt, pepper and a little sugar. When well mixed add two tablespoons browned butter.
MRS. WALTER A. PRIESTER.
organization: Trinity Cathedral (Davenport, Iowa). Trinity Guild; Trinity Cathedral (Davenport, Iowa). St. Margaret's Guild

title: Sill Salad (Herring Salad)
full_text:
One (1) salt herring, soaked over night, boned and cubed. 4 medium sized boiled potatoes cubed, 8 medium sized boiled beets cubed, 2 medium sized peeled apples, cubed, 2 dill pickles, cubed, 2 cups cold lean roast beef, cubed. Place above ingredients in stone crock, season with 1 teaspoon sugar and pour over enough white vinegar to cover. This makes about 2 quarts.
MRS. HENRY ARP.
organization: Trinity Cathedral (Davenport, Iowa). Trinity Guild; Trinity Cathedral (Davenport, Iowa). St. Margaret's Guild

title: Fish Mold
full_text:
Soften one envelope of Knox's gelatin. Add dissolved gelatin to 3/4 cup boiled salad dressing and a cup of salmon, tuna or crab meat. Add salt and paprika and 2 teaspoons vinegar. Mold and chill and cut in slices to serve. Garnish with lemon.
MRS. ISAAC DEUTSCH.
organization: Trinity Cathedral (Davenport, Iowa). Trinity Guild; Trinity Cathedral (Davenport, Iowa). St. Margaret's Guild

title: Potato Salad
full_text:
12 boiled red potatoes
1 lg. strong white onion or several green onions with red onion
12 hard-boiled eggs
Hellmann's Real mayonnaise
Dice all ingredients and mix together with salt and pepper, to taste. Add mayonnaise, enough until salad is quite moist. Do not add anything else to the above. Place in one container or more. Refrigerate.
Betty Woodke

full_text:

1/2 tsp. salt
1 c. Miracle Whip
1 1/2 T. onion, chopped
1/4 c. tarragon vinegar
1 lg. head of cabbage
1/2 c. vegetable oil
1 diced green pepper
Mix together sugar and Miracle Whip. Add vinegar, vegetable oil, salt and finely-chopped onion. Pour over shredded cabbage. May also add diced green pepper. This will keep 10 days.
Carolyn Stille

full_text:
1 1/2 lb. shredded cabbage
1/3 c. vinegar
1 tsp. salt
1 c. whipping cream (do not whip)
2/3 c. sugar
Place shredded cabbage in a covered dish and refrigerate several hours. Mix ingredients in order given, 30 minutes before serving. Chill and serve.
Kathleen Lichtenberg
cookbook_title: Schaller Chamber cookbook: celebrating 50 years of pop corn days, Schaller, Iowa

title: Grandma Wandrey's Tomato Juice Salad
full_text:
2 sm. pkg. lemon Jello
2 T. grated onion
2 c. hot tomato juice
2 T. green pepper
1/2 c. hot water
1 tsp. horseradish
1 c. celery
1/4 c. vinegar
1 c. cucumber
1/2 c. Miracle Whip
In medium-size bowl, dissolve Jello in tomato juice and water. When dissolved, add celery, cucumber, onion, green pepper, horseradish and vinegar. Fold in Miracle Whip when it starts to set.
Patty Miller

title: Mixed Vegetable Salad
full_text:
1 1/2 c. bite-sized raw cauliflower
1 1/2 c. bite-sized broccoli
1 1/2 c. thick-sliced carrots
1 med. green pepper
1 1/2 c. crookneck squash, sliced
1/2 c. sliced onion
1 1/2 c. broken green beans
DRESSING
2/3 c. salad oil
1/2 tsp. salt
1 1/4 tsp. grated lemon peel
1/2 tsp. sugar
1/2 c. lemon juice
1/2 tsp. basil leaves
1/4 tsp. black pepper
1 tsp. prepared mustard
In an electric fry-pan, bring to boil 1 inch salted water and cook cauliflower for 3 to 4 minutes, remove and cool. Then add carrots, cook for 5 to 6 minutes, remove and cool. Next, add squash and cook for 3 minutes, remove and cool. Next add the green beans, cook for 5 minutes and remove and cool, and last, add broccoli and cook for 4 minutes, remove and cool. Combine the cauliflower, carrots, onion and green pepper. Combine the dressing ingredients and pour over the combined vegetables and chill. Thirty minutes before serving, add the green beans and broccoli. Chill.
I have added more basil, salt and lemon juice to the dressing.
Jo Ann Jacobson

full_text:

1 box cherry tomatoes
1 pkg. fresh broccoli
1 btl. Italian oil dressing (Zesty Italian)
1 jar mushrooms (opt.)
1 can ripe olives
1 pkg. dry Italian creamy dressing (Hidden Valley or other)
1 green pepper
3 to 4 green onions
Cut vegetables in bite-size pieces in a large bowl. Sprinkle dry dressing over the top. Toss. Then pour oil dressing on top and toss. Chill. Let stand 2 hours, tossing several times. Will keep a week.
Carolyn Stille

1 can red beans, rinsed & drained

1/2 c. water
2 T. prepared mustard

1 1/2 c. sour cream
1/4 tsp. onion salt

full_text:
3 boxes macaroni rings
1 btl. Dorothy Lynch salad dressing
1 cucumber
1 green onion
1 carrot
1 radish (opt.)
Celery
1 jar pimentos
1 jar mushrooms
Sliced black olives
1 c. salad dressing
2 lb. ham
Cook macaroni rings as directed on package. Dice all vegetables in small pieces. Mix with Dorothy Lynch dressing; let stand. Add salad dressing. Add vegetables, a little less or more, according to your liking.

full_text:

1 c. sunflower seeds
1/2 c. browned bacon pieces
2 c. chopped celery
2 c. red grapes
3/4 c. toasted, slivered almonds
DRESSING: 1 c. Miracle Whip or Spin Blend salad dressing
2 T. vinegar
1/4 c. sugar
In a bowl, put broccoli, sunflower seeds, bacon, celery, grapes and almonds. Mix salad dressing, vinegar and sugar. Pour over other ingredients. Toss. To toast almonds, put on a shallow baking pan in a 350° oven for 15 minutes. Stir occasionally.
Gladys Huseman

full_text:

1 sm. red onion, chopped fine
1/2 c. raisins
8 to 10 slices cooked bacon, crumbled
1/2 c. Hellmann's lite mayonnaise

1 c. chopped cauliflower
1 green onion, chopped
1 c. chopped celery
Cashews (opt.)

DRESSING:

1/2 c. sour cream

full_text:

1 lb. bacon
Layer:
1 head lettuce, broken into pieces
1/2 head cauliflower, cut into pieces
1 onion, sliced in rings
Bacon, on top
Mix together:
1 c. mayonnaise
1/3 c. Parmesan cheese
1/4 c. sugar
Spread over salad and refrigerate 24 hours or overnight. Toss just before serving.

full_text:
Iceberg, red leaf & Boston bibb lettuce
1 c. diced celery
1 bunch green onions, chopped
1 can mandarin oranges, drained
1/4 c. almond slices
2 T. sugar
DRESSING:
2 T. tarragon vinegar
4 T. oil
2 T. sugar
1/2 tsp. salt
1/4 tsp. white pepper
1/4 tsp. almond extract
Wash and tear lettuce into bite-size pieces. Place almonds in nonstick skillet. Add sugar and stir over low heat until coated and brown. Pour on foil to cool. Break apart.
Dressing: Shake all dressing ingredients in a glass jar. Chill until serving time.
I usually prepare almonds and mix the dressing the day before. Just before serving, toss the almonds with the greens and toss with the chilled dressing.
Eleanor (Hase) Bahr

full_text:

1 pkg. frozen peas, cooked
Onion, to taste, chopped fine
1 can water chestnuts, sliced fine*
1 pt. Hellmann's mayonnaise
2 T. sugar
1 lb. bacon, fried crisp & crumbled
1 1/2 c. finely-shredded Cheddar cheese
Layer into a 9x13-inch pan. Sprinkle with Cheddar cheese. Refrigerate at least 2 hours or overnight.
*May substitute chestnuts with chopped hard-boiled eggs.
Mary Cole

1 bunch green onions, diced small (tops & all)
1 c. celery, diced
1 sm. can water chestnuts
1/2 c. chopped green pepper
Dressing:
1/2 c. oil
1/2 c. sugar
1/4 c. vinegar
1 T. soy sauce
Oriental mix pack from noodles
Toast noodles until light brown (break up before putting them in oven). Add noodles and dressing and toss just before serving.
Virginia Burhop

title: Cabbage Lemon Salad
full_text:
6 c. finely-chopped cabbage
1/3 c. water
2 med. carrots, finely shredded
1/2 c. sugar
1 sm. onion, grated
1/4 tsp. mustard seed
1 sm. green pepper, chopped (opt.)
1 tsp. salt
3/4 c. salad oil
1 tsp. celery seed
1/3 c. vinegar
1 pkg. lemon Jello
Combine vegetables and pour oil over them. Let stand while you heat other ingredients, except Jello. When mixture boils, add Jello and stir until dissolved. Cool. Pour over vegetables. Mix well. Refrigerate overnight.
Salad will keep 2 to 3 weeks in tightly-covered container.

full_text:

Bacon bits

1/2 c. olive oil

1 head Napa (Chinese) cabbage, finely chopped
2 T. sesame seeds
1/4 c. sliced almonds
5 green onions, chopped

1/2 c. sugar
1/4 c. rice vinegar
1/2 c. oil
1/2 tsp. salt
In sauté pan, brown Ramen noodles, sesame seeds and almonds in butter (watch carefully, they burn easily!). Mix dressing ingredients together and add to chopped cabbage and onions. Toss all together just before serving.
Yield: 8 to 10 servings.

full_text:
1 pkg. cole slaw mix
1/4 c. oil
2 pkg. Ramen noodles, not cooked (chicken flavor)
2 pkg. Lipton vegetable soup mix (dry)
1 bunch green onions
1 c. sunflower seeds
1/3 c. vinegar
1 c. cashews
1/2 c. sugar
Mix slaw mix, noodles and onions together. Put vinegar, sugar, oil and soup mix on cole slaw 1 to 2 hours before serving. Add sunflower seeds and cashews 1 minute before serving.

full_text:
1 chicken breast, cooked & shredded
1/2 head cabbage, shredded
2 or more chopped green onions
2 T. sesame seeds
1 pkg. Ramen noodles (chicken flavor)
1/2 c. almonds, slivered & toasted
Toast almonds in 300° oven for 10 minutes. Mix first 5 ingredients together. Crush noodles and add. Right before serving, toss with 1/2 to 1 package seasoning from Ramen noodles.

1 T. sugar
1 T. MSG Accent (opt.)
1/2 c. oil
1/4 to 1/2 tsp. pepper, coarse grind
1 tsp. salt
3 T. rice vinegar
Mix well.

1/2 c. sliced almonds
1 c. chopped celery
3 T. sugar
2 whole green onions, chopped
1/2 head iceberg lettuce
1 (11 oz.) can mandarin oranges, drained
1/2 head romaine lettuce
DRESSING:
1 T. chopped parsley
1/2 tsp. salt
2 T. sugar
Dash of pepper
2 T. vinegar
1/4 c. vegetable oil
Dash of Tabasco
In a small pan over lowheat, cook almonds and sugar, Stirring constantly, until almonds are coated and sugar dissolved. Watch carefully, as they burn easily. Cool almonds and store in airtight container. Mix all dressing ingredients and chill. Mix lettuce, celery and onions. Just before serving, add almonds and oranges. Toss with dressing. Yield: 4 to 6 servings.

1 sm. onion
1 pepper, chopped

1 tsp. Worcestershire sauce
1 c. sugar
Salt, to taste
3/4 c. vinegar
Pepper, to taste

1 head lettuce
4 tomatoes, diced
1 red onion, sliced thin
1 lg. avocado, diced
1 can black olives, halved
1 1/2 to 2 lb. grated Cheddar cheese
Tortilla chips
Taco salad dressing (recipe below)
Cut up head of lettuce and place in a large bowl. Add tomatoes, onion, avocado and black olives. Brown meat with garlic powder, salt, onion powder, chili powder and cumin. Drain and cool. Crush chips into bite-size pieces. Serve on plate: salad, meat, shredded cheese, chips and dressing.

1 c. oil
1/2 c. vinegar
1/2 c. ketchup
2 tsp. salt
2 T. + 1 tsp. sugar
1/8 tsp. garlic powder
Picante sauce, to taste (about 1/4 c.)

title: Mediterranean Couscous Salad
full_text:
1 1/2 c. whole wheat couscous
1/3 c. (about 10) sun-dried tomatoes (not packed in oil)
2 1/2 c. boiling water
DRESSING:
2 T. chopped fresh dill
2 garlic cloves, pressed or minced
3 T. fresh lemon juice
1 T. olive oil
3 T. balsamic vinegar
VEGETABLES:
1/2 c. diced celery
1 c. peeled & diced carrots
Salt, to taste
1 c. diced zucchini
Ground black pepper, to taste
1/2 c. diced red bell peppers
1 tomato, diced
1/2 c. diced red onions
A few fresh parsley or dill sprigs
Place the couscous in a pot, pour 1 3/4 cups of the boiling water over it, cover and set aside. Place the sun-dried tomatoes and 3/4 cup of boiling water in a covered heat-proof bowl. While the tomatoes soften, whisk together the dressing ingredients and set aside. Uncover the couscous and fluff it with a fork. Blanch the carrots, zucchini and bell peppers in boiling water until just tender. Drain well. Drain and chop the sun-dried tomatoes. In a large bowl, combine the couscous, sun-dried tomatoes, blanched vegetables, red onions, celery and dressing. Add salt and pepper. Chill for at least 1 hour. Add the diced tomatoes just before serving. Top with parsley or dill sprigs.
Grated Chevre or feta cheese makes an excellent garnish. Avoid overcooking the vegetables in this dish, they should be tender, but still brightly colored.

title: Mandarin Almond Salad
full_text:
4 T. sugar, divided
1/8 tsp. pepper
1/2 c. slivered almonds
1/8 tsp. hot pepper sauce
1/4 c. vegetable oil
1 bunch red leaf lettuce, torn
2 T. vinegar
1 can mandarin oranges, drained
1 T. minced, fresh parsley
1 sm. red onion, sliced
1/2 tsp. salt
In a small skillet, melt 3 tablespoons sugar over low heat. Add almonds. Stir until coated. Cool and break into small pieces. Set aside. In a jar, combine oil, vinegar, parsley, salt, pepper, hot pepper sauce and 1 tablespoon sugar. Shake well. Just before serving, combine lettuce, oranges, onion and almonds in a large salad bowl. Shake dressing. Pour over salad and toss. Yield: 4 to 6 servings.
Karen Wilder-Bailey

title: Microwave Salad
full_text:
2 (20 oz.) cans chunk pineapple
4 bananas
2 (11 oz.) cans mandarin oranges
Maraschino cherries, drained
2 sm. boxes vanilla pudding (cook & serve)
Drain pineapple and oranges and set fruit aside. Put pudding in juice, mix well and microwave until thick, stirring occasionally. Add pineapple and oranges, and refrigerate. Put bananas and cherries in just before serving.
Cherries are for color, so can use as many as you like.
"Sukey" Whitney

full_text:
Just lettuce alone!

full_text:
1 (6 oz.) box Jello (any flavor)
1 can mandarin oranges, drained
1 lg. ctn. Cool Whip
Chopped nuts
1 lg. can crushed pineapple, drained
Mix dry Jello into Cool Whip. Mix in remaining ingredients.
Leila Grohe

title: Frozen Salad
full_text:
1 med. can crushed pineapple
1 sm. pkg. mini marshmallows
1 box red Jello
Mix all the ingredients and let set overnight. The next day, crush 1 package of mixed buttermints and fold in a medium container of Cool Whip. Pour into your mold and freeze.
Juanita Johnson

title: Autumn Apple Salad
full_text:
1 (20 oz.) can crushed pineapple, with juice
8 oz. cream cheese
1 c. diced, unpeeled apples
2/3 c. sugar
1/2 c. chopped walnuts
1 (3 oz.) pkg. lemon Jello
Boil crushed pineapple (with juice) and sugar for 3 minutes. Remove from heat and stir in Jello until dissolved. Add cream cheese and stir until well blended. Cool and fold in apples and walnuts. Chill well.
Susie Mayou

title: Mom's Fruit Salad
full_text:
1 (13 1/2 oz.) can pineapple tidbits
2 bananas
1 can mandarin oranges (drain & save juice)
1 c. mini marshmallows
1/2 c. nuts
3 apples, diced
DRESSING:
1/2 c. sugar
2 eggs, beaten
2 T. flour
1/2 tsp. butter
Pinch of salt
1 c. juice from drained fruit
Cook dressing until thickened. Cool and fold into 8 ounces of Cool Whip. Pour over fruit, mix well and chill.
Jackie Mentzer

title: Delicious Fruit Salad
full_text:
2 bananas, sliced
1 c. orange juice
1 unpeeled red apple, chopped
1/2 c. sugar
1 unpeeled green apple, chopped
2 T. cornstarch
Sections of 2 oranges
1 tsp. grated lemon peel
1 (8 oz.) can pineapple chunks, drained
Juice of 1 lemon
2 tsp. grated orange peel
1 pt. strawberries, sliced
Layer fruit in a glass bowl. Combine orange juice, sugar and cornstarch in a saucepan. Cook over medium heat until thickened, stirring constantly. Stir in lemon juice and grated peels. Pour hot sauce over layered fruit. Chill, covered, for 1 hour or longer. Yield: 20 servings.
Lori Nehring

title: Fruit Salad
full_text:
1 (14 oz.) can pineapple tidbits, juice & all
2 soft kiwi, peeled & chopped
1 c. seedless grapes (cut up after measured)
1 (11 oz.) can mandarin oranges, juice & all
2 firm apples, chopped
3 med. (part green) bananas, chopped
1 (6 oz.) box sugar-free Jello (red)
Mix all ingredients together. (No substitutes.) This will keep in the refrigerator for 2 weeks.
Good for diabetics.
Ruth Borcherding
cookbook_title: Schaller Chamber cookbook: celebrating 50 years of pop corn days, Schaller, Iowa
organization: Schaller (Iowa). Chamber of Commerce

title: Fruit Salad
full_text:
2 (20 oz.) cans pineapple tidbits
Apples
2 (11 oz.) cans mandarin oranges
Fruit cocktail or peaches
1/2 jar red cherries, chopped
1 1/4 c. pineapple juice
3 bananas
1 lg. box vanilla pudding (cook & serve)
 Grapes
Drain pineapple, reserve the juice and combine with pudding. Cook until it thickens. Cool. Drain other fruits, do not use this juice. Combine all fruit in bowl, then pour pudding mixture over fruit and stir until coated. Refrigerate.
This salad can be made a day ahead, and the pineapple juice prevents the bananas from changing color.
Darlene Franzkowiak

title: Fruit Salad
full_text:
2 pkg. lemon Jello
4 lg. bananas
4 c. boiling water
Mini marshmallows (white)
2 sm. cans crushed pineapple, drained
TOPPING:
Pineapple juice, add water to make 1 c.
1/2 c. sugar
2 T. flour
1 c. real cream, whipped
1 egg, beaten
Grated cheese
Mix Jello in boiling water. Let cool, then add remaining ingredients.
Topping: Cook sugar, flour, egg and pineapple juice until thickened; let cool. Add whipped cream. Pour over salad. Sprinkle cheese on top.
Kathleen Lichtenberg

title: Fruit Salad
full_text:
1 pkg. vanilla pudding (cook & serve)
1 can mandarin oranges
1 can pineapple chunks
1 T. tapioca
1 banana, sliced
1 T. frozen concentrated orange juice
Frozen peach slices (original)
Mix tapioca, juices and pudding. Let stand 5 minutes, stir and cook on medium heat until it comes to full boil. Remove and cool. Add 1 teaspoon vanilla. Can add maraschino cherries for color, if desired.
Takes 10 to 15 minutes to make. Use sugar-free pudding for diabetics.
Yield: 6 to 8 servings.
Arlene Grundmeier

title: Golden Flecked Salad
full_text:
1 pkg. lemon Jello
1/2 tsp. pineapple flavoring
2 c. boiling water
1 c. grated carrots
1 (3 oz.) pkg. Philadelphia cream cheese
1 c. crushed pineapple, drained
1/2 c. cream, whipped, or 1 c. whipped topping
50 mini marshmallows
1/2 tsp. lemon flavoring
Dissolve Jello in hot water. Add softened cheese and marshmallows. (May be left whole.) Add flavoring. Cool until it starts to set, then add pineapple and carrots. Fold in the whipped cream.
Marie Werner
cookbook_title: Schaller Chamber cookbook: celebrating 50 years of pop corn days, Schaller, Iowa

title: Celebration Salad
full_text:
2 (3 oz.) boxes tapioca pudding
1 (8 oz.) ctn. whipped topping
1 (3 oz.) box orange Jello
1 can mandarin oranges, drained
3 c. warm water
1 (8 oz.) can crushed pineapple
Combine tapioca pudding, orange Jello and water. Bring to a boil on top of the stove. Cool. Stir in oranges and pineapple. Fold in whipped topping.
Lucille Tuel

title: Marshmallow Fruit Bowl
full_text:
1 (20 oz.) can pineapple tidbits
2 T. all-purpose flour
1 (15 oz.) can chunky mixed fruit
2 eggs, lightly beaten
1/4 c. lemon juice
1/2 c. whipped topping
1/4 c. sugar
1 c. mini marshmallows
Drain pineapple and mixed fruit. Reserve 1 cup of juice. Set fruit aside. In a saucepan, combine lemon juice, sugar, flour and reserved fruit juice. Stir until smooth. Cook and stir until heated through. Add a small amount of hot liquid to eggs. Return all to pan. Bring to a boil. Boil and stir for 2 minutes. Cool completely. Fold in whipped topping. Fold in marshmallows, pineapple and mixed fruit. Transfer to a serving bowl. Yield: 10 (1/2-cup) servings.
Fernetta Siebrecht

title: Cherry Pie Salad
full_text:
1 can cherry pie filling
1 can condensed milk (Eagle Brand)
1 sm. can crushed pineapple or tidbits
1/2 pt. whipped cream or Cool Whip
1 c. mini marshmallows
Drain pineapple. Add pie filling and condensed milk. Mix well. Add whipped cream or Cool Whip, and marshmallows.
You can freeze this salad.
Missy Kestel

title: Dorothy's Cherry Salad
full_text:
1 (3 oz.) box raspberry Jello
1 c. crushed pineapple, not drained
1 (21 oz.) can cherry pie filling
2 c. boiling water
1 (3 oz.) box lemon Jello
1/2 c. whipping cream, whipped
1 (3 oz.) pkg. cream cheese
1 c. mini marshmallows
1/2 c. mayonnaise
1/4 c. chopped pecans
Dissolve raspberry Jello in 1 cup of boiling water. Let cool and add the can of cherry pie filling, pour into an 8-inch pan. Let stand in the refrigerator until partially set. Dissolve lemon Jello with 1 cup boiling water; cool. Beat together cream cheese and mayonnaise. Gradually blend with the lemon Jello. Add the pineapple, fold in the whipped cream and marshmallows. Spread over the chilled raspberry layer. Sprinkle with the chopped pecans. Chill until well set.
Carol Maymon

title: Cherry Salad
full_text:
2 boxes cherry Jello
1 can cherry pie filling
2 c. hot water
TOPPING:
1/2 pt. sour cream
2 c. mini marshmallows
Mix the Jello with the 2 cups hot water and put the pie filling in. Mix sour cream and marshmallows and let set overnight. The next day you can whip this and then spread it over the Jello pie filling mixture.
Doris Aylward

title: Cranberry Salad
full_text:
1 pkg. cranberries
1 (15 oz.) can pineapple, crushed or tidbits
1 (8 oz.) pkg. mini marshmallows
1 c. sugar
1/2 c. nutmeats (opt.)
2 c. diced apples
1 pkg. Dream Whip
Grind cranberries. Add marshmallows and sugar. Stir well. Let stand all day or overnight. Stir occasionally. Add apples, pineapple and nutmeats. Fold in prepared Dream Whip. Keep refrigerated.
Lorraine Drey

title: Holiday Cranberry Salad
full_text:
1 lb. cranberries
2 pkg. raspberry Jello
2 lg. peeled apples
3 c. hot water
2 c. sugar
Grind cranberries and apples in food chopper. Add sugar and let stand until sugar is dissolved. Dissolve packages of Jello in hot water, let cool. Stir in cranberry mixture. Refrigerate. Stir once in a while until it begins to set.
Hellen Boisen

title: Cranberry Delight Salad
full_text:
1 pkg. raspberry Jello
1 1/2 c. sugar
1 pkg. lemon Jello
1 c. nutmeats
3 c. boiling water
1 to 2 c. white grapes
2 c. ground, fresh cranberries
2 c. diced celery
1 sm. can crushed pineapple, undrained
Mix all together and pour into mold. Serve on lettuce leaves with mayonnaise. Yield: 12 servings.
Bertha Blewitt

title: Cranberry Salad
full_text:
1 lb. cranberries
4 c. boiling water
1/2 lb. marshmallows
1 1/2 c. whipping cream
1 c. crushed pineapple, drained
1 T. salad dressing
3 pkg. red Jello (I prefer raspberry)
1/2 c. toasted pecans
1 c. sugar
Grind cranberries and mix with the sugar; let stand for 8 to 10 hours. Dissolve Jello in hot water. Whip cream and add the salad dressing. After the Jello has cooled, fold in the whipped cream and the rest of the ingredients. Pour into a greased 9x12-inch pan, or a ring mold or large bowl. For molded salad, add 3/4 of a package of Knox gelatin.
Jo Ann Jacobson

title: Cranberry Salad
full_text:
1 pkg. cranberries
1 sm. can crushed pineapple
1 sm. pkg. marshmallows
2 pkg. Dream Whip (or Cool Whip)
1 c. sugar
Nuts (opt.)
Grind cranberries. Add marshmallows and sugar. Let stand in refrigerator at least 1 hour or overnight. Then add pineapple and prepared Dream Whip or Cool Whip.
This was given to me many years ago from a dear friend.
Neoma Pyle

title: Cranberry Salad
full_text:
2 pkg. strawberry gelatin
1 lg. can mandarin oranges, mashed
2 c. boiling water
Add juice to make 1 cup boiling liquid. Add 1 can whole cranberry sauce and one 12 or 16-ounce package of frozen strawberries. Dissolve Jello in boiling water. Add strawberries when still hot. Add the rest of the ingredients. Chill until set.
Wanda Hansen

title: Cranberry Salad
full_text:
1 lb. frozen cranberries
1 1/4 c. sugar
Grind together and mix and let stand 2 hours.
Then mix:
1 lb. mini marshmallows
1 (20 oz.) can crushed pineapple, drained
1 (12 oz.) ctn. Cool Whip
Nuts (opt.)
May be frozen. Tastes better when stands a day or so.

full_text:

1 (20 oz.) can crushed pineapple, undrained
8 oz. Cool Whip
2 c. mini marshmallows
1/2 c. chopped nuts
Mix all ingredients together and refrigerate.
Goldie Koehne

title: Orange Sherbet Salad
full_text:
1 pkg. orange Jello
1 pt. orange sherbet
1 c. boiling water
2 cans mandarin oranges, drained
Dissolve Jello in boiling water. Stir in orange sherbet until melted. Refrigerate Jello and sherbet mixture until partially set, then stir in mandarin oranges. Chill until firm.
Betty Franken

title: Lemon Salad
full_text:
1 pkg. lemon Jello pudding (not instant); cook as directed
1 pkg. dry Jello (mix into pudding)
Add:
1 c. water
1 can drained mandarin oranges
Chill until set.
Jan Ronfeldt

title: Luscious Lemon Salad
full_text:
2 (3 oz.) pkg. lemon gelatin
1 (8 oz.) can crushed pineapple, well drained
2 c. boiling water
1 (12 oz.) can Mountain Dew
1 (22 oz.) can lemon pie filling
1 c. mini marshmallows
1 (8 oz.) ctn. frozen whipped topping
In a large bowl, dissolve gelatin in boiling water. Add Mountain Dew and stir well. Stir in marshmallows, drained pineapple, and 1/2 of the pie filling. Pour into a 2-quart oblong dish. Chill until set. Thaw topping. Fold together topping and remaining pie filling. Spread evenly over chilled gelatin mixture.
Jan Witte

title: Lemonade Salad
full_text:
CRUST:
1 c. powdered sugar
55 Ritz crackers
1 stick margarine
Crush crackers. Melt butter. Mix all 3 ingredients together. Set aside 1 cup of the mixture. Press the rest into the bottom of a 9x12-inch pan.
FILLING:
1 (6 oz.) can frozen lemonade
12 oz. Cool Whip
1 can Eagle Brand condensed milk
Blend together. Pour over crust. Sprinkle remaining 1 cup crust over the top. Refrigerate at least 1 hour before serving.
Laura Foell

title: Lime Jello Salad
full_text:
1 sm. pkg. lime Jello
6 to 8 oz. cream cheese
1 c. hot water
1 (15 oz.) can crushed pineapple
Dissolve Jello in water. Whip in cream cheese. Add crushed pineapple. Works well in a loaf pan.
Gertie Burmester
cookbook_title: Schaller Chamber cookbook: celebrating 50 years of pop corn days, Schaller, Iowa
organization: Schaller (Iowa). Chamber of Commerce

title: Orange Pudding Salad
full_text:
2 pkg. vanilla tapioca pudding
1 can mandarin oranges
1 pkg. orange Jello
1 can pineapple tidbits
Drain syrup from fruits, adding enough water to make 3 1/2 cups. Add to pudding mix and cook until it thickens. Add orange Jello to hot pudding and cool slightly. Add oranges and pineapple and pour into large bowl. Add 1/2 of an 8-ounce carton of Cool Whip. Mix together and set in refrigerator until ready to serve. Yield: 6 to 8 servings.
Very good.
Tracy Whetstone
cookbook_title: Schaller Chamber cookbook: celebrating 50 years of pop corn days, Schaller, Iowa
organization: Schaller (Iowa). Chamber of Commerce

title: Raspberry Junket
full_text:
1/4 c. butter
8 oz. cream cheese
1/4 c. sugar
2 pkg. frozen raspberries
1 1/2 c. graham cracker crumbs
1 pkg. raspberry-currant junket
1/2 c. powdered sugar
4 oz. Cool Whip
2 c. Cool Whip
Combine butter, crumbs and sugar; press into a 9x13-inch pan. Bake in 350° oven for 8 minutes. Add 2 cups Cool Whip to softened cream cheese and powdered sugar; mix well. Spread over cooled crumbs. Thaw raspberries. Use juice plus water to make 1 3/4 cups liquid for junket; cook and cool. Fold in raspberries and pour over cream cheese mixture. Spread Cool Whip over top. Cool, preferably overnight.
Judy Denney
cookbook_title: Schaller Chamber cookbook: celebrating 50 years of pop corn days, Schaller, Iowa
organization: Schaller (Iowa). Chamber of Commerce

title: Rhubarb Salad
full_text:
2 c. chopped rhubarb
1 c. boiling water
1/2 c. water
1/2 c. drained, crushed pineapple
1/2 c. sugar
2 c. chopped apples
1 (3 oz.) pkg. strawberry Jello
1/4 c. nuts, chopped
Mix rhubarb, 1/2 cup water and sugar. Cook and cool. Mix Jello and boiling water. Cool. Mix drained pineapple, apples and nuts. Mix all together, making sure it's cool before adding it all together.
Darla Koth
cookbook_title: Schaller Chamber cookbook: celebrating 50 years of pop corn days, Schaller, Iowa
organization: Schaller (Iowa). Chamber of Commerce

title: Strawberry Tapioca Fruit Salad
full_text:
2 cans chunk pineapple
1 sm. pkg. strawberry Jello
2 cans mandarin oranges
2 sm. pkg. cook & serve vanilla pudding
1 lg. can sliced peaches
4 sliced bananas
3 T. tapioca
Fresh or frozen whole strawberries
Use 4 cups fruit juice in saucepan. Add dry Jello, dry pudding mix and tapioca. Cook until thick; cool. Add fruit and chill. Makes a large salad.
Kris Hansen
cookbook_title: Schaller Chamber cookbook: celebrating 50 years of pop corn days, Schaller, Iowa
organization: Schaller (Iowa). Chamber of Commerce

title: Strawberry Tofu Salad
full_text:
1 (4 oz.) pkg. sugar-free strawberry Jello
1 c. nonfat yogurt
1/4 tsp. vanilla
3/4 c. water
1/2 c. finely-chopped strawberries
5 oz. silken tofu
1 banana, sliced
Sprinkle the Jello over the boiling hot water. Stir to dissolve the gelatin. Put the tofu, yogurt and vanilla into a blender and whirl until very smooth, stopping to scrape down the sides as necessary. Pour the puréed tofu mixture into the gelatin mixture and stir everything in to blend well. Cover and refrigerate for at least 1 hour. Fold in the strawberries and the banana. Pour mixture into a 9-inch square pan. Refrigerate until firm. To serve, cut the salad into 1-inch cubes and serve with sliced fruit on the sides.
Laura Foell
cookbook_title: Schaller Chamber cookbook: celebrating 50 years of pop corn days, Schaller, Iowa
organization: Schaller (Iowa). Chamber of Commerce

title: Red-Top Salad
full_text:
FIRST LAYER:
1 pkg. red Jello
2 c. boiling water
SECOND LAYER:
1 pkg. lemon Jello
2 c. boiling water
10 lg. marshmallows
1 c. whipping cream (not Cool Whip)
1 c. crushed pineapple, drained
1/2 c. salad dressing
1/2 c. nuts
1/2 c. chopped celery
First Layer: Mix together. Pour into a 9x9-inch pan and refrigerate until set.
Second Layer: Mix lemon Jello with 2 cups boiling water. Add the marshmallows and stir until dissolved. Refrigerate until partially set, then add the whipping cream. Whip it together. Mix in rest of ingredients. Pour on top of red Jello and refrigerate until set. To serve, cut into squares. Serve, red-side up, on lettuce leaves.
Leila Grohe
cookbook_title: Schaller Chamber cookbook: celebrating 50 years of pop corn days, Schaller, Iowa
organization: Schaller (Iowa). Chamber of Commerce

title: Red-Top Salad
full_text:
1 pkg. strawberry Jello
1/2 lb. cheese, cut fine or diced
2 pt. hot water
1/2 c. nutmeats, chopped
1 pkg. lemon Jello
1/4 c. salad dressing
10 marshmallows
1 c. whipped cream
1 sm. can crushed pineapple
Prepare strawberry Jello using 1 pint of hot water; set aside. Prepare lemon Jello using second pint of hot water. While hot add marshmallows to lemon Jello. Partially cool and add the next 5 ingredients. Put in a cake pan, let set, or at least chill. When set, pour strawberry Jello on top and let set. Serve on lettuce with a small amount of salad dressing.
Marie Werner
cookbook_title: Schaller Chamber cookbook: celebrating 50 years of pop corn days, Schaller, Iowa
organization: Schaller (Iowa). Chamber of Commerce

title: Orange Ritz Salad
full_text:
CRUST:
1 stick oleo, melted
60 Ritz crackers, crushed
3 T. sugar
MIDDLE:
1 can sweetened condensed milk
1 (6 oz.) can frozen orange juice, thawed
1 (8 oz.) ctn. Cool Whip
2 cans mandarin oranges, drained
Crust: Mix and save 1/4 cup for top. Press remaining into a 9x13-inch pan. Middle: Mix all ingredients and pour on top of crust. Top with remaining crumbs. Refrigerate overnight.
Jan Ronfeldt
cookbook_title: Schaller Chamber cookbook: celebrating 50 years of pop corn days, Schaller, Iowa
organization: Schaller (Iowa). Chamber of Commerce

title: Good Salad
full_text:
1/2 c. sugar
1 c. grated cheese
1 can crushed pineapple, undrained
1 c. nutmeats
1 ctn. Cool Whip
1 pkg. orange or lemon Jello
Boil sugar and undrained pineapple together for 3 minutes. Dissolve 1 package of Jello (orange or lemon) in a short cup of boiling water. Add to pineapple mixture. Chill well (but not set). Add grated cheese and nutmeats. Fold in Cool Whip.
Bertha Blewitt
cookbook_title: Schaller Chamber cookbook: celebrating 50 years of pop corn days, Schaller, Iowa
organization: Schaller (Iowa). Chamber of Commerce

title: Frozen Fruit Salad
full_text:
Three cups fruit—pineapple, bananas, oranges, sliced peaches. Either black cherries or strawberries for color. 1 cup mayonnaise, 1 cup cream, whipped, 2 teaspoons gelatin, soaked in 2 tablespoons cold water and melted over hot water. Fold fruit into dressing. Freeze.
Mrs. H. C. Richmann.
organization: St. Paul's Evangelical Lutheran Church (Waverly, Iowa). Orphans' Aid Society

title: Sunshine Salad
full_text:
One package lemon Jello, 1 cup hot water, 1 cup cold water, 1 tablespoon lemon juice, 1 can pineapple cut in strips, about 4 or 5 carrots, shredded. Add the pineapple and carrots when Jello is cool. May be made in a dripping pan or molds. Pineapple juice may be used instead of cold water.
Mrs. W. G. Voecks.
organization: St. Paul's Evangelical Lutheran Church (Waverly, Iowa). Orphans' Aid Society

title: Nutted Cream Salad
full_text:
One heaping tablespoon Plymouth Rock gelatin dissolved in 1/2 cup of pineapple juice, set in a dish of hot water to dissolve it. Beat stiff one pint of cream. When cold add gelatin, 1/2 cup of candied cherries, 1 cup of walnut meats (not too fine) and 1 cup of pineapple cut in small pieces, and flavor with vanilla. Put in cold place or ice box to set.
Mrs. Rowray.
organization: St. Paul's Evangelical Lutheran Church (Waverly, Iowa). Orphans' Aid Society

title: Glazed Cranberries
full_text:
Two cups cranberries, 1 cup sugar. Wash cranberries, put in heavy aluminum sauce pan, cover with sugar, cook 20 minutes. Remove the cover and shake slightly to cool and glaze the surface.
Mrs. A. G. Wenninger.
organization: St. Paul's Evangelical Lutheran Church (Waverly, Iowa). Orphans' Aid Society

title: Cranberry Salad
full_text:
One-half pound cranberries, 1/2 cup sugar, 1 cup grapes, 1/2 cup pineapple, 2 small apples. Wash and grind cranberries, add sugar and grapes which have been halved, then peel apples and grind them also, then pineapple (crushed is best). If this salad is kept in cool place it keeps for days.
Mrs. Wm. Schoof.
organization: St. Paul's Evangelical Lutheran Church (Waverly, Iowa). Orphans' Aid Society

title: Raw Cranberry Salad
full_text:
One quart cranberries, 4 apples, 2 whole oranges, yellow skinned, 1 1/2 cups sugar. Grind all and mix; always use thick yellow skinned ones. 1/4 cup nuts.
Mrs. A. G. Wenninger.
organization: St. Paul's Evangelical Lutheran Church (Waverly, Iowa). Orphans' Aid Society

title: Herring Salad
full_text:
One dozen herring soaked in water over night, about 1/2 pound boiled veal, 2 onions, 2 pickles, 2 hard boiled eggs, 2 boiled red beets. Skin and bone herring, put all through grinder and add pepper to taste. Mix well, then add 1 cup vinegar, or more if necessary for moist salad.
Emma Laube.

title: Shrimp Salad
full_text:
One can shrimp (remove black ring from outside) cut fine, 3 hard boiled eggs diced, 1/2 cup shredded cabbage, 1 small onion grated, 1 tablespoon minced parsley, 1/2 cup celery diced, 1/2 cup shredded carrots, 1/4 cup cucumber diced. Salt to taste. Mix with mayonnaise, place in refrigerator and chill.
Mrs. F. C. Koch.

title: Mock Shrimp Salad
full_text:
Take equal parts of grated raw carrot and hard boiled egg. Season with salt and pepper, add mayonnaise.
Mrs. M. D. Benedict.

title: Tuna Fish Salad
full_text:
One-half cup diced celery, 1 hard boiled egg, 1 can tuna fish, about 6 pimento olives, pinch of salt. Mix the above with salad dressing that has been thinned with cream. Serve on lettuce leaf. Shrimp may be used in place of tuna fish if desired.
Mrs. Harold Gruben.

title: Kidney Bean Salad
full_text:
One can kidney beans, 3 hard boiled eggs, 1/2 cup diced cheese (white), 1/2 cup diced celery, 1/2 cup chopped sweet pickles. Mix well and combine with mayonnaise. (Miracle Whip is a good dressing to use with this salad or Best Foods mayonnaise.)
Mrs. Bertha Patzer.

title: Bean Salad
full_text:
One quart cooked green beans (or wax beans), 1 onion, 1 cup thick sour cream, 1 tablespoon prepared mustard, 2 tablespoons sugar, 1 tablespoon vinegar, 1/8 teaspoon salt. Combine string beans and chopped onions. Beat remaining ingredients with egg beater until like whipped cream; mix with beans and garnish with paprika.
Mrs. Bertha Patzer.

title: Tomato Jelly Salad
full_text:
One can tomato juice. Celery, green pepper, 1 package lemon Jello, English walnuts. Dilute tomato juice with water, making two cups, and heat. Pour over lemon Jello and cool. Serve tomato jelly plain, or if desired add chopped celery and green pepper, also walnuts. This makes eight molds.
Mrs. A. P. Colburn.

title: Tomato Aspic
full_text:
One can tomatoes, 2 or 3 stalks celery, 1 small onion, 1 bay leaf. Cook five minutes. Strain and add 2 tablespoons vinegar. Have 1 pint liquid, add water if necessary. Heat to boil. Pour over 1 package lemon Jello. Add dash of red pepper and salt. Mold in ring and put celery or cabbage salad in center. Nice with shrimp or chicken salad.
Mrs. R. Eldon Laird.

title: Tomato Salad
full_text: Dissolve package of lemon Jello in 1 cup of hot water and 1 cup of strained tomatoes, add 1 tablespoon of lemon juice. When cool and beginning to thicken, pour over 1/2 cup finely chopped carrots, 1 cup finely chopped cabbage or celery or both, 1 chopped pimento. Serve on crisp lettuce and garnish with salad dressing and a dash of paprika. —Mrs. Louise Vogt.

title: Cabbage Slaw Salad
full_text:
To about 1 quart cabbage, cut fine on slaw cutter, add 1 or more tablespoons sugar, sprinkle a little salt on it, 3/4 cup vinegar and 4 or 5 slices bacon that have been shredded and fried till crisp. Add the bacon hot; pour off the fat, save for future use. Add a little of the vinegar to bacon settlings in pan, heat and pour over cabbage. Rest of vinegar add cold. Mix well. Head lettuce cut in 1 inch cubes is very good made that way. Leaf lettuce, endive and (celery, cabbage or lettuce). Also string beans, either wax or green, boiled in salt water and drained. Raw chopped onion may be added if desired
Mrs. A. G. Wenninger.

title: Mixed Vegetable Salad
full_text:
Shred cabbage, dice celery and green pepper, grate carrot and small onion, cut up tomatoes, cucumbers and radishes. Mix all with salad dressing to which has been added some whipped cream. Serve on lettuce leaf. Nice as a hostess salad.
Mrs. A. F. Droste.

title: Pineapple-Cheese Salad
full_text:
One medium sized can grated pineapple, 3/4 cup sugar, juice of 1/2 lemon. Cook ten minutes. Add to the above: 1 package lemon Jello, dissolved in 1 cup boiling water. Cool, when quite thick fold in 1 cup of whipped cream and 1 cup grated cheese. Serve with whipped cream salad dressing.
Mrs. E. G. Engelbrecht.

title: Stuffed Green Peppers
full_text:
Six green peppers, 1% cup rice, 11, cup canned tomatoes, 2 teaspoons salt, 1 cup cheese cut in small pieces. Wash the peppers, cut a slice from stem and end of each pepper, remove the seeds. If peppers are large, cut each one in half, lengthwise. Wash rice. On a low burner cook it in 14 cup of tomatoes until mixture is dry. Remove from fire and add the remainder of tomatoes and cheese. Fill the peppers with rice mixture, place them in a baking dish or pan. Pour enough boiling water into the dish or pan to cover the bottom of it and place it in the oven and bake about one hour.
